about.p: Together, we’re traveling into the future — deep down into the dark depths of the ocean.
Climate change has altered the habitat there as well. Many deep-sea corals are struggling to survive under the new conditions.
But then, a new species of deep-sea coral is discovered. It has developed a special defense mechanism that helps it cope with the effects of climate change.
What might this deep-sea coral look like? How does it protect itself?

about.lead: Draw your deep-sea coral of the future and show what kind of protection it has developed.

about.p: Whether biologically accurate, completely made up, unusual, or totally bizarre — anything goes. Let your imagination run wild.

about.lead: There are no right or wrong answers!

step: 1. Grab a sheet of paper and a pen.
Draw how a coral might protect itself from the effects of climate change. Let your imagination run wild!
It’s up to you whether you want to write your name on the sheet. If you do write your name, it will become the scientific name of your imaginary coral.
4. Put the completed piece of paper in the box.

about.p: Every specimen goes back to the same template: Desmophyllum pertusum, a cold-water stony coral that builds reefs in cold, dark depths far below 1000 metres.
Participants coloured that template in and thought it further — giving the coral shields, cooling systems, weapons, legs, or simply new colours. Each drawing was then turned into a 3D model.

Every specimen has been given an invented environment here: the sea it would have needed for exactly this adaptation to make sense. The years arrange these scenarios into one possible sequence — they are narrative, not forecast.
The variety names are invented too. Where the artist is known, the coral carries their name; otherwise the name describes the most striking adaptation.
